questions.q: To whom did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to declare the words of this covenant?
questions.a: Yahweh said to declare them to each man of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

questions.q: Why would the people be cursed?
questions.a: They would be cursed if they did not listen to the words of the covenant.

questions.q: To whom was this covenant given?
questions.a: The covenant was given to Israel’s ancestors.

questions.q: When was the covenant given?
questions.a: It was given the day Yahweh brought the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.q: What is the oath Yahweh swore to the ancestors?
questions.a: He swore that he would give them the land flowing with milk and honey.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to proclaim in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
questions.a: He told him to proclaim the words of the covenant and tell the people to obey them.

questions.q: Why did God bring all the curses in the covenant against the people?
questions.a: He brought them because the people did not obey the covenant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he had found among the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: He said he had found a conspiracy among them.

questions.q: What was the conspiracy among the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: They refused to listen to Yahweh and worshiped other gods.

questions.q: When Yahweh brings disaster on the people and they call out to him, how will he answer them?
questions.a: He will not listen to them.

questions.q: What will happen when the people of Judah and Jerusalem cry out to their gods for help?
questions.a: Their gods will not save them.

questions.q: How many incense altars to Baal were made in Jerusalem?
questions.a: The people made an altar to Baal on every street.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh command Jeremiah not to pray for the people?
questions.a: He was not to pray because Yahweh would not listen.

questions.q: Why will the people’s sacrifices not help them?
questions.a: The sacrifices cannot help them because they have done evil and then been happy about it.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to his people, whom he compared to a beautiful olive tree?
questions.a: He said he would send enemies to attack them and destroy them.

questions.q: What wicked act have the people committed?
questions.a: They have given offerings to Baal.

questions.q: What did Yahweh reveal to Jeremiah?
questions.a: He revealed that his enemies were plotting to kill him.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah’s enemies plan to do to him?
questions.a: They planned to kill him so that no one would remember him.

questions.q: What part of man does Yahweh examine?
questions.a: He examines the heart and the mind.

questions.q: What were the people of Anathoth telling Jeremiah they would do if he kept prophesying in the name of Yahweh?
questions.a: They said they would kill him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the people who wanted to kill Jeremiah?
questions.a: He said their young men would die by the sword and their children would die from famine.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the people of Anathoth?
questions.a: He said none of them would remain alive because he would bring disaster on them.

commentary.text: The disobedient Jews reproved. (Jer. 11:1-10) Their utter ruin. (Jer. 11:11-17) The people would be destroyed who sought the prophet's life. (Jer. 11:18-23)

Jer. 11:1-10 God never promised to bestow blessings on his rational creatures, while they persist in wilful disobedience. Pardon and acceptance are promised freely to all believers; but no man can be saved who does not obey the command of God to repent, to believe in Christ, to separate from sin and the world, to choose self-denial and newness of life. In general, men will hearken to those who speak of doctrines, promises, and privileges; but when duties are mentioned, they will not bend their ear.

Jer. 11:11-17 Evil pursues sinners, and entangles them in snares, out of which they cannot free themselves. Now, in their distress, their many gods and many altars stand them in no stead. And those whose own prayers will not be heard, cannot expect benefit from the prayers of others. Their profession of religion shall prove of no use. When trouble came upon them, they made this their confidence, but God has rejected it. His altar shall yield them no satisfaction. The remembrance of God's former favours to them shall be no comfort under troubles; and his remembrance of them shall be no argument for their relief. Every sin against the Lord is a sin against ourselves, and so it will be found sooner or later.

Jer. 11:18-23 The prophet Jeremiah tells much concerning himself, the times he lived in being very troublesome. Those of his own city plotted how they might cause his death. They thought to end his days, but he outlived most of his enemies; they thought to blast his memory, but it lives to this day, and will be blessed while time lasts. God knows all the secret designs of his and his people's enemies, and can, when he pleases, make them known. God's justice is a terror to the wicked, but a comfort to the godly. When we are wronged, we have a God to commit our cause to, and it is our duty to commit it to him. We should also look well to our own spirits, that we are not overcome with evil, but that by patient continuance in praying for our enemies, and in kindness to them, we may overcome evil with good.
